def count_eulerian_circuits(n, edges):
    """Count Eulerian circuits through vertex 0 of a directed multigraph.

    The graph has n vertices, labelled 0..n-1 (1 <= n <= 10), and its edges
    are given as a list of 1 to 40 pairs (u, v), each a directed edge from u
    to v (self-loops u == v and repeated parallel edges are allowed).

    An Eulerian circuit here is an ordering (e_1, e_2, ..., e_m) of ALL m
    input edges such that the head of e_i equals the tail of e_{i+1} for
    every i < m, the tail of e_1 is vertex 0, and the head of e_m is
    vertex 0.  Edges are distinguishable by their position in the input
    list, so two parallel copies of the same (u, v) pair may be swapped to
    produce a different circuit.  Return the exact number of such orderings
    as a Python int (it may be astronomically large; the count must be
    exact).  If no such ordering exists (unbalanced degrees, vertex 0
    untouched by any edge, or the edges do not form one connected circuit
    through 0), return 0.

    >>> count_eulerian_circuits(3, [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)])
    1
    >>> count_eulerian_circuits(1, [(0, 0), (0, 0)])
    2
    >>> count_eulerian_circuits(3, [(0, 1), (1, 0), (0, 2), (2, 0), (1, 2), (2, 1)])
    6
    >>> count_eulerian_circuits(4, [(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 1)])
    0
    """
